description:

author: IGN
description:
In today's Daily Fix:
Pearl Abyss' highly-anticipated open-world action-RPG Crimson Desert is finally out, and it's causing the publisher's stock to drop. Reviews for the game have been mixed-to-positive, currently sitting at a 78% on Metacritic, and that wiped out around 30%—about $13 USD—from the company's stock. Our own review-in-progress was a little tepid, calling out the game's promise but also the myriad of bugs. In other news, a bug update to Counter-Strike 2 is changing how the game handles reloads. The game will be adopting a Helldivers 2-esque reload mechanic where you lose any remaining rounds in the clip you're tossing out, instead of 'topping off' when you put in a fresh mag. And finally, Sony is making some branding changes to the PlayStation Network, specifically getting rid of that moniker entirely.

#IGN #Gaming
title: Crimson Desert's Reviews Cause Publisher's Stock Price to Plummet 30% - IGN Daily Fix

author: IGN
description:
Crimson Desert is finally here, and its massive open world of Pywel is as beautiful as it is overwhelming. With total freedom granted almost immediately, it’s easy to get lost in choice paralysis or miss out on game-changing upgrades hidden right under your nose. From finding a powerful secret shield at the very start to unlocking essential traversal abilities like flight and telekinesis, we’ve spent countless hours uncovering the systems the game doesn't explicitly explain. Whether you're looking to expand your inventory, rob the local bank without getting caught, or even recruit a loyal pet to loot enemies for you, this guide covers the twelve essential things you should do first to master the early hours.

In this Crimson Desert gameplay guide, we break down the best early-game strategies to help you level up fast and survive the "blessing and a curse" of its unfathomable map. Learn how to locate Abyss Nexus fast travel points, where to find the Backalley Merchant for masks and key
title: Crimson Desert: 12 Things to Do FIRST

author: IGN
description:
Crimson Desert is big. Yes, it has an insanely large map size. Yes, there are over 70 bosses to defeat, and yes… there is fishing. Basically, if you’re wondering if a particular game mechanic is in Crimson Desert, the answer is probably yes in some shape or form. And with that immense size and breadth of options, comes a lot of quirks, systems, and time-saving tricks it either doesn’t tell you, or flashes on-screen so quickly during the deluge of information that you may not see at all. Here are 14 Things Crimson Desert Doesn’t Tell You, or that are really easy to miss.

Conversely, NVIDIA showed off its DLSS 5 tech by giving Resident Evil Requiem, Starfield and Hogwarts Legacy some makeovers that might be a little too noticeable, and which most of the internet seems to look more like AI slop than next gen video games. author: IGN
description:
So, Nvidia just revealed DLSS 5, its new AI graphics tech that uses generative systems to “enhance” video games with more photo-realistic effects, and I’m not going to worry about mincing my words here: I think it looks shit. Yes, we’ve barely seen a minute of it in action, but if what’s teased is where technology giants think the future of graphics tech in games is going, then I’m afraid I’m out.

With games like Resident Evil Requiem, Hogwarts Legacy, and Starfield shown with DLSS 5 on and off, it seems more like characters are rocking an Instagram AI filter, like they've been yass-ified. This obviously will have an impact on the art teams in charge of creating these beautiful worlds and detailed models. What do you think? Are you happy with how DLSS 5 looks? 

#DLSS5 #AI #NVIDIA
title: Nvidia's DLSS 5 Is a Slap in the Face to the Art of Video Game Design
